The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 17.07.2023.

2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 17.07.2023 at about 08.15 a.m., petitioner was walking on the side of the road, carefully, observing all traffic rules, proceeding near Apollo Pharmacy, 13th Cross, Basavanapura Main Road, Bangalore, at that time rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-R-0556 rode the same in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner.
Due to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body.

Immediately, petitioner was shifted to Tirumala Orthopedic and pediatric Hospital wherein he treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses,
conveyance, food, transport and other charges.
The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident she was heal and healthy and aged about 48 years, the petitioner was working as Attender at Cambridge College and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner is not able to do her job and hence lost her earnings.
Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notice, both the respondents appeared before this court and filed their respective written statements.

The respondent No.1 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent riding of the offending Eswaramma A vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 27 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196857117/
2 motorcycle.

sentences.text: Further, this respondent seeks protection U/s 134(c), 156(6) of M. V. Act.

Further, this respondent admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and policy was inforce as on the date of accident and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.

Further this respondent submits that, as per the police documents the alleged accident was occurred mainly due to the negligence of the petitioner as she was crossing the road where there is no zebra crossing lines.
Hence, the negligence is on the part of the petitioner only.

Further this respondent submits that, the rider of the motorcycle did not possess valid and effective driving license at the time of accident and owner knowing fully has entrusted the said vehicle to him.

The respondent No.2 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and submitted that, the petitioner attempted to cross the main road where there is no Zebra crossing and without observing any traffic rules and regulations and dashed the offending motorcycle.
Further, this respondent proceeded towards the jurisdictional police station, reported the incident and they refused to take the complaint of the rider/owner of the motorcycle.
Further, both the respondents denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
The petitioner colluding with the police filed the false case.
By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessor framed the following issues are as under:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, on 17.07.2023 at about 8.15 a.m., when the petitioner was proceeding as a pedestrian near Apollo Pharmacy, 13th cross,
Basavanapura main road, Bengaluru, at that time motorcycle bearing Reg. No.
KA-53-R- 0556 ridden by its rider in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life, without following any traffic rules and dashed to the petitioner and caused the accident and as a result,
petitioner sustained injuries as alleged by her?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or Award?

5. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, she has got herself examined as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.15 and also examined Dr. Nagaraj B. N as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.16 and 17 and closed their side.
On the other hand, respondents examined witnesses as RW.1 and RW.2 and in all got marked the documents at Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.6.

6. Heard arguments of both the sides and perused the materials placed on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under; Issue No.1: In the Affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.

8. ISSUE No.1:

sentences.text: The petitioner has contended that on the above said date, time and place she met with accident and sustained grievous injuries occurred due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of offending vehicle.
9. The petitioner who is injured in this accident has got examined herself as PW-1 by reiterating the averments made in the petition.
She has produced the documents at Ex.P.1 to 15.

Ex.P.1 is the FIR,
Ex.P.2 is the complaint, Ex.P.3 is the Charge-sheet, Ex.P.4 is the spot mahazar, Ex.P.5 is the Sketch,
Ex.P.6 is the IMV Report, Ex.P.7 is the Wound Certificate, Ex.P.8 is the Police intimation, Ex.P.9 is the notice u/s 133 of M. V. Act, Ex.P.10 is the Reply notice, Ex.P.11 is the discharge summary,
Ex.P.12 is the medical bills, Ex.P.13 is the Prescriptions, Ex.P.14 is the notarized copy of Aadhar card and Ex.P.15 is the Resignation Letter.

10. On going through the materials, it could be seen that on 17.07.2023 at about 08.15 a.m.,
petitioner was walking on the side of the road, carefully, observing all traffic rules, proceeding near Apollo Pharmacy, 13 th Cross, Basavanapura Main Road, Bangalore, at that time rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-R-0556 rode the same in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner.
Due to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body.
Immediately, petitioner was shifted to Tirumala Orthopedic and pediatric Hospital wherein she treated as inpatient.
Accordingly, the K. R. Puram Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.224/2023.

After completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 279 and 338 of IPC.
11.
The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person.
It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence to shameful disregard of safety of others.
In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act.
Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something.
In short, it is want of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do.

The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-R-0556.
12.

As we know evidence in any Summary Proceedings, "The act of Negligence" will have to be assessed on the basis of broad preponderance of probabilities and degree of proof required is not one of beyond reasonable doubt, as it is insisted in criminal case for "The Negligent Act".
13. The certified copy of the First Information (First information statement/s complaint in common para-lace) lodged before the K. R. Puram Traffic Police has been marked as Ex.P2.
On receiving the First Information, the Station House Officer chose to register a case in Crime No. 224/2023.
The said certified copy of First Information Report (F.I.R.) is marked as Ex.P.1.

sentences.text: During the Course of examination-in-chief, petitioner got marked Ex.P.1 to 10 are the only documents, which are to be scrutinized to arrive at conclusion- whether the accident was owing to the negligent manner of riding by the rider of offending motorcycle.

The Ex.P.4 and Ex.P.5 (spot panchanama and Sketch), clearly discloses the place of accident and that the police, after registering the First Information, held investigation and filed the Ex.P.3, Charge- Sheet against the rider of motorcycle U/s. 279 and 338 of IPC.

The Ex.P.6 i.e., certified copy of the IMV Report discloses that,
the accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle in question.
15.

On the other hand, respondents examined one eye- witness to the accident as RW.1 and employer of petitioner as RW.2 and in all got marked documents at Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.6.
16.
In this case, respondent No.2 i.e., rider of the offending vehicle examined as RW.1.
In his examination-in- chief he depose that, the petitioner suddenly entered to the road and in that place there is no Zebra cross.
Further he depose that, the accident is caused due to sole negligence of petitioner.
During his cross-examination he depose that, since 15 years he has been using the Basavanpur road to reach his office and there was no zebra crossing on the said road.

17. In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
18.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for petitioner submits that, the accident is caused due to sole negligence of respondent No.2 i.e., rider of offending vehicle.
Hence, he argued that, both respondents are liable to pay compensation.
On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.1 argued that, the accident was caused due to the negligent act of the petitioner.

Further he argued that, the petitioner was crossing the road at there was no Zebra crossing and accident occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner also and he submitted that, consider 25% negligence on the part of petitioner.

In support of his line of argument he relied upon the following decisions of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, i.e., MFA NO. 1192/2018 between Thippeshappa and others And M.D, KSRTC and another, MFA NO.2259/2013 C/w MFA NO.4572/2018 between M.D, KSRTC And Sri.
Parameshwar C. Aralaguppi and another.
19. In the light of above arguments and materials available on record, this court once again perused the documents as well as oral evidence.
Admittedly, the accident is not disputed, the only contention of the petitioner is that, the accident is occurred on account of negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle.
On the other hand, it is the contention of the Insurance company that, the petitioner himself has suddenly entered the road and cross the road where there was no zebra cross to cross the road.
As per the Final report the accident is caused due to sole negligence of rider of offending vehicle.
On going through the hand-sketch map produced at Ex.P.5, it goes to show that accident is caused at the middle of the road.
The said fact is not disputed by both parties.

On going through the chief as well as cross-examination of rider of offending vehicle it goes to show that, in his chief examination he depose that, there was no zebra crossing mark on the spot of the accident but in his cross-examination he depose that, since 15 years he has been using the Basavanpur road to reach his Eswaramma A vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 27 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196857117/
5 office and there was no zebra crossing on the said road.

sentences.text: However, on going through the cross-examination of PW.1 she herself deposed in her cross-examination that, there is zebra cross infront of her school.

So, this admission itself goes to show that, even in the presence of zebra cross that too infront of her school she crossed the road from one side of the road to another, where there was no zebra cross.
If petitioner should have used the zebra crossing instead of crossing the road as shown in the Ex.P.5 she could have avoided the accident.
Further, as per the hand-sketch map the accident is caused in the middle of the road.

Hence, having regard to the above facts and circumstances this court opine that, the location/spot of the alleged RTA and the nature of the vehicles would enable this tribunal to fix the contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner at 10% and the remaining negligence which would be 90% upon the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-53- R-0556.
Hence, the petitioner has utterly failed to prove that, the alleged accident has occurred due to the sole negligent act on the part of rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-R- 0556.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
20. ISSUE No.2:

The petitioner in her evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident she was shifted to Tirumala Orthopedic and pediatric Hospital, wherein she was admitted as inpatient and she took treatment.
Petitioner has stated in the petition that, she is undergoing deep mental shock, severe pain and sufferings.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
21. PAIN AND SUFFERING:
In the petition as well as in her evidence PW.1 deposed that,

immediately after the accident she was shifted to Tirumala Orthopedic and pediatric Hospital,
wherein she took treatment as an inpatient from 17.07.2023 to 20.07.2023.
The petitioner has produced the discharge summary marked at Ex.P.11 wherein it is mentioned that the petitioner was admitted in the Tirumala Orthopedic and pediatric Hospital, Bangalore for 03 days.

entities.text: Tirumala Orthopedic and pediatric Hospital, Bangalore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He has produced the wound certificate marked at Ex.P.7, which reveals that, petitioner has sustained closed fracture neck of the left femur and the doctor has opined that the injury is grievous in nature.

Hence,
it is clear that during the above said period the petitioner suffered lot of pain and inconvenience.
Considering all these aspects this tribunal has granted Rs.50,000/- under the head of pain and suffering.
22. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that she has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
In support of her plea, she has produced 11 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.12 to the tune of Rs.1,85,995/-.
Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,85,995/-
towards medical expenses.

23. LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID UP PERIOD:
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.11 Discharge summaries issued by Tirumala Orthopedic and pediatric Hospital, Bangalore, it reveals that, the petitioner took treatment from the said hospital from 17.07.2023 to 20.07.2023 i.e. for 03 days.
Hence, at least 2 months is required to recover from the accidental injuries.

It is the further contended that, the injured petitioner was working as Attender in Cambridge Eswaramma A vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 27 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196857117/

sentences.text:
The respondents examined one Lakshmancharry who is the office incharge at Cambridge College, K. R. Puram,
Bangalore as RW.2 who has produced the Authorization Letter, Certificates and Pay-slips of petitioner which are marked at Ex.R.2 to Ex.R.6.
In his examination-in-chief he depose that, petitioner was working as Attender at Cambridge college, K. R. Puram, Bangalore and since July-2023 she remained absent.
During his cross examination he depose that, his school authorities deposited salary for the month of August and September 2023 to the account of petitioner on the ground of compensation.
As per the payslip for the month of July to September she is getting salary of Rs.20,000/- per month.
The learned counsel for insurance company argued that, she is still working at Cambridge college as Attender.
But in order to substantiate his argument, he has not produced any documents before this court.
Hence, in view of above discussion, this court opine that, she is getting salary of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Hence, 2 months is to be considered as loss of income.
Hence, she is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under this head.
24. Towards loss of future earning capacity on account of Permanent Physical Disability-

The petitioner to prove her disability, she has produced the evidence of Dr. Nagaraj B. N in order to substantiate the same, PW.2 who has opined that, total physical disability of left lower limb at 52%
and that of whole body disability at 17%.
Admittedly, the PW.2 is not a treated doctor.

Same was admitted by the PW.2 during his cross examination, the relevant evidence of the PW.2 reads as follows :
"     
   ."
He was sworn that, petitioner has got 17% disability to the whole body but he was not issued the disability certificate.
It is quite but natural that to help the petitioner doctor will give exaggerated disability.
In cross-examination of PW.2 i.e., Doctor, he depose that, there is no problem to petitioner to work by sitting.
But as per the records petitioner is working as Attender.
So after the accident she is unable to work as earlier to the accident.
However, looking to the nature of the injuries it is proper to came to conclusion that there is 12% of disability to the petitioner.
25. Before proceeding on merits of the claim the age of the petitioner /injured has to be determined.
Ex.P.14 is the Aadhar Card of the petitioner, wherein his DOB is mentioned as 01.01.1975 and accident took place in the year 2023.
Accordingly, I assess his age as 48 years at the time of this accident.
As per the ruling reported in AIR 2009 SCW page-3014 between SARLA VERAMA AND OTHERS VS DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND OTHERS, the relevant multiplier applicable is '13'.

27. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The petitioner was aged about 48 years at the time of accident, she has sustained grievous injuries.
It shows that she found difficulty in doing day to day works.
She might have suffered lot of pain and loss of amenities and comforts in life.
Therefore, considering the age, nature of injuries and percentage of disability, Rs.20,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of future amenities and happiness.
28. TOWARDS FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES :
The petitioner has claimed towards future medical expenses.
The doctor who has been examined as PW.2 has suggested another surgery for the revision arthroplasty after 10 years.
But he has not given any estimation of the said surgery.
By keeping nature of the injuries sustained, as she is bound to suffer medical problems in future and cannot every time depend upon Government hospital.
Hence, under this head Rs.30,000/- is awarded.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:
1 Pain and sufferings Rs. 50,000/-
2

Medical expenses Rs. 1,85,995/-
3 Loss of earnings during laid Rs. 40,000/-
up period 4 Loss of future earning Rs. 3,74,400/-
capacity 5 Nutritious food and Rs. 30,000/-
attendant charges 6 Loss of future amenities and Rs. 20,000/-
loss of happiness.

7 Future Medical Expenses Rs. 30,000/-
Total Rs. 7,30,395/-
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.7,30,395/- under various heads.
29. LIABILITY:
As discussed in Issue No.1, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-R-0556 and petitioner in the ratio of 90:10.

The respondent No.1 issued the policy to the offending vehicle valid from 31.07.2022 to Eswaramma A vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 27 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196857117/
8 30.07.2023 and accident occurred on 17.07.2023, thus the policy was in-force as on the date of accident.

sentences.text: As discussed above, this Tribunal opine that, petitioner has contributed the negligence for the cause of accident to an extent of 10%.
So, if 10% is deducted, out of total compensation of Rs.7,30,395/-, it comes to Rs.6,57,355/-.
Thus the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.6,57,355/-.
Hence, in view of above discussion, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, respondent No.1 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.2 owner.
30. INTEREST:

As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
By relying on the aforesaid decision,
6% interest awarded to the petitioners in the present case on hand.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.
31. ISSUE No.3:
In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
:ORDER:
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I.M.V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.6,57,355/- with interest @ 6%
p.a., on Rs.6,27,355/- (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 being insurer of the vehicle involved in an accident is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the above compensation amount with interest thereon before Tribunal within two months from the date of this award.
In the event of deposit of total compensation amount, entire amount shall be released in favour of petitioner.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon, disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.
2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated:19.08.2019.

The petitioner is hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contains compulsorily photograph of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.

Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Adhar Card.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person.
It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence to shameful disregard of safety of others.
In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act.
Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something.
In short, it is want of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do.
The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-R-0556.
12.
As we know evidence in any Summary Proceedings, "The act of Negligence" will have to be assessed on the basis of broad preponderance of probabilities and degree of proof required is not one of beyond reasonable doubt, as it is insisted in criminal case for "The Negligent Act".
In this case, respondent No.2 i.e., rider of the offending vehicle examined as RW.1.
Further he depose that, the accident is caused due to sole negligence of petitioner.
As per the Final report the accident is caused due to sole negligence of rider of offending vehicle.
Hence, having regard to the above facts and circumstances this court opine that, the location/spot of the alleged RTA and the nature of the vehicles would enable this tribunal to fix the contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner at 10% and the remaining negligence which would be 90% upon the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-53- R-0556.
